description.narrative: CMI!’s vision is a gender-equal and just world where all women, girls, and non-binary, gender non-conforming, trans and intersex people enjoy their rights fully and live to their full potential. Our role in bringing about this vision is to support movements to be resilient and leverage their power to create change from local to global and from global to local, thereby engendering systemic and sustainable change at all levels.

In order for feminist civil society movements to be strong and autonomous39 (an ambitious achievement in itself), self-led WHRDs and WROs go through three intermediate steps - resulting in CMI!’s output (see section 4 and Annex 1, our Results Framework). WHRDs and WROs must be: RESOURCED with the knowledge, resources, and skills for impact, including for L&A. COORDINATED to be able to organise together to articulate priorities and take collective action, including amplifying voices through alliances between structurally excluded movements, linking with more mainstream movements where possible. RESILIENT by having resources, networks, strength and holistic security in place to sustain their work including in the face of backlash and closing civic space, build broader support bases, and expand their work.

Our five-year strategic objective is: political actors, societal actors and donors at local, national, regional and global levels take action to recognise, protect and fulfil the human rights of all women, girls, and non-binary, gender non-conforming, trans and intersex people as a result of strong and autonomous feminist movements holding them to account.

During 2021, RUF continued to be active in several decision-making platforms and working groups to raise the visibility of the sex workers’ rights movement among funders and to increase effectiveness and reach of funders. Below are highlights of this work:RUF participated in a webinar organised by Funders Concerned About AIDS (FCAA) to discuss the findings on the launch of their Annual Resource Tracking Report. On 1 June, FCAA published an article introducing RUF’s Coordinator and discussing funding for sex workers’ rights. On 2 June (International Sex Workers’ Day), the Count Me In! 2.0 Consortium, including RUF, co-signed a statement to CEDAW members [Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women] condemning the discriminatory and harmful measures in CEDAW’s General Recommendation N. 38.RUF signed the Affirmation of Feminist Principles statement reaffirming core feminist principles including the recognition of sex work as work.RUF joined the Global Alliance for Sustainable Movements reference group - an emerging multi-stakeholder initiative focused on “exponentially increasing, sustaining and improving financial and political support for women’s rights and feminist organizations and movements.RUF joined the Global Philanthropy Project’s Responding to Anti-Gender Ideologies Task Force whose goal is to “strengthen and expand philanthropic support for a robust, coordinated, and well-informed response to ’anti-gender ideology’ forces.RUF organised an interactive Teach In with Share-Net Netherlands, Sekswerk Expertise, and WO=MEN Dutch Gender Platform targeting the latter’s members and SRHR and women’s rights organisations. The Teach In was attended by approximately 20 representatives of organisations. RUF endorsed Funders Concerned About AIDS’s Racial Justice Principles. Funders Concerned About AIDS (FCAA) released a Briefing Paper to help make the case for greater investment in HIV-related intermediaries including a case study on RUF. In 2021, RUF was involved in 11 convenings and networks such as the Sex Work Donor Collaborative and Human Rights Funders NetworkRed Umbrella Fund created or defended space 25 times in 2022, including continuing to implement its digital space (4: a website and 3 social media platforms). In its tenth year, RUF also gained more influence and recognition in the philanthropic field with seats on the Accountability Circle of the Participatory Grantmakers Community of Practice and a decision by the membership of the Sex Work Donor Collaborative to give RUF a permanent seat on its Steering Committee. In 2022 - the Fund's tenth anniversary, Red Umbrella Fund launched a new website in English, French, Russian and Spanish. The website provides information on the fund’s processes and showcases our learning from a decade of resourcing and accompanying sex worker-led organisations worldwide. The website also includes information on the organisations we have supported, as well as an extensive catalogue of resources for funders and sex workers.In its tenth year, RUF also gained more influence and recognition in the philanthropic field with seats on the Accountability Circle of the Participatory Grantmakers Community of Practice and a decision by the membership of the Sex Work Donor Collaborative to give RUF a permanent seat on its Steering Committee. Other highlights of the Fund’s Funder Advocacy work in 2022 include: Red Umbrella Fund (RUF) continued to be active in several decision-making platforms and working groups to raise the visibility of the sex workers’ rights movement among funders and to increase effectiveness and reach of funders. Below are highlights of this work: RUF co-organised through the Count Me In! 2.0 Consortium (CMI!) a formal side-event at the Commission on the Status of Women #66 on Strengthening labour rights through cross-movement collaborations with the Count Me In! 2.0 Consortium. RUF’s LinkedIn passed 1,000 followers! RUF was featured in Comic Relief’s report on their experience supporting feminist movements released in May (in English). RUF participated in RightsCon 2022. On 09 June 2022, Mama Cash and RUF held a session entitled “Open source: improving digital security for criminalized communities” attended by 36 attendees and whose recording remains available for registered participants. RUF participated in and presented in two sessions at the 2022 International AIDS Conference. The Sex Work Donor Collaborative (SWDC) organised a briefing for funders and activists on how sex workers are particularly affected by the anti-rights movement.. RUF organised a presentation to the National Postcode Lottery on funding and sex workers’ rights attended by around 40 staff members. RUF also gained more influence and recognition in the philanthropic field with seats on the Accountability Circle of the Participatory Grantmakers Community of Practice and a decision by the membership of the Sex Work Donor Collaborative to give RUF a permanent seat on its Steering Committee.RUF Secretariat members attended Changing Spaces Changing Spaces and participated on panels at Women Deliver and Harm Reduction International Conference. RUF created and participated in a series of three webinars in collaboration with SWDC & NSWP regarding the changes to the funding fo sex workers' rights after the withdrawal of OSF from the space. Outcome from 2024 RUF engaged in donor and funders paces including CSW, HRFN, AIDS Conference, the GATE Trans Pre- Conference, AWID, Numun Fund's Trueque (Feminist Technologies gathering), SWDC member conviening, FCAA's board meetings, ASWA's Donor Round Table, PGM Evaluation community conversation, the Netherlands' NGO briefing with Civil Society."RUF participated in spaces with networking partners including: FCAA Summit Washington; RightsCon in collaboration with Mama Cash and SWAN; CSW NYC 2025 including a plennary with SWDC, New Moon, IPPF and various regional network representatives as well as the Dutch Civil Society meeting; On Crisis and Care Global Convening co-hosted by Sister Funds for Urgent Action; European Donors convening organised by FCAA to respond in the cut to HIV funding by the Dutch and US governments; Human Rights Council in collaboration with CMI, SRI, ESWA, and NSWP.RUF also added to its global strategy by funding SWAN which in 2025 helped support their work across the region and globally. SWAN, together with the Sexual Rights Initiative (SRI), co-organized a side event titled “Sexual Rights at the UN HRC: Past, Present, and Future” during the 60th Session of the Human Rights Council in September 2025. Outcome results from 2024 RUF contributed to input to the Guide to Human Rights for Sex Workers commissioned by Special Rapporteur Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng, Special Rapporteur on the right of everyone to the highest standard of physical and mental health (SR health), the Independent Expert on protection against violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity (IE SOGI), and the UN Working Group on discrimination against women and girls (WGDAWG), advocated along with nine feminsit partnerships to shape the Dutch Ministy of Foreign Affair's funding framework. RUF collaborated through the Sex Work Action Group (SWAG) of CMI! to create a library of submissions from sex worker-led organisations and their allies to respond to the anti-rights call by UN Special Rapporteur on Violence Against Women. In June, NSWP and Sexual Rights Initiative (SRI) led a campaign to increase sex worker visibility at the 56th UN Human Rights Council Meeting – an effort to combat the negative report and to uplift the human rights-based policies on sex work. ADD RUF's GLOBAL WORK FOR 2025 SWAN submitted a report to the UN Special Rapporteur on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association, contributing to the 80th thematic report to the UN General Assembly. The submission outlined the legal and funding barriers faced by sex worker-led organizations in eight countries across the CEECA region: Hungary, North Macedonia, Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Armenia, and Ukraine. They also worked to support organisations coping with security threats.
